# Geometric-mean affine buffers: an exact optimum with a nonuniform limit

This is an actual convex-body calibration, not an OC counterexample. It proves that an attained interior multiplier optimum need not keep the physical buffers small as epsilon tends to zero. Its unequal two-point base violates the strict proper-minor quotas; no failure under those additional hypotheses is asserted.

## 1. Actual body and buffer

In R times R take the trapezoid

    C=conv({0} times [−1/2,1/2], {1} times [−3/4,3/4]).

Its only integer fibers have lengths a=1 and b=3/2. Thus M=5/2. Their within-fiber covariance and the invariant normalization constant are

    Sigma=(a^3+b^3)/(12M)=7/48,
    c^2=Sigma/M=7/120.

For an interval of length V centered at zero, the projective energy at y is

    E_V(y)=V−4y^2/V,     |y|<=V/2.

Let ell be any positive affine function on [0,1], with endpoint values ell_a,ell_b. Impose weighted geometric-mean normalization

    ell_a^(2/5) ell_b^(3/5)=1,

or equivalently ell_a^2 ell_b^3=1. At a source (i,y), the invariant buffer shifts every nonvertical cap threshold outward by

    delta_i(y)=epsilon*c*sqrt(ell_i E_V(y)).

Pure integer caps receive no shift. This is precisely the d=1 aligned buffer f_ell=(ell E/M)^(1/2), with the within-fiber covariance norm.

## 2. All-normal, all-source formula

For either endpoint base, an arbitrarily steep integer tilt isolates its fiber without changing its own trace. Every ambient cap contributes a nonnegative amount from the other fiber. Consequently the exact buffered depth at (i,y) is

    b_epsilon(i,y)=min{V, V/2−|y|+delta_i(y)}.                 (1)

The term V is the isolating pure-integer cap. The two continuous orientations yield the other term. Both |y| and the energy formula show that its fiber maximum is

    Q_i=min{V, V/2+epsilon*c*sqrt(ell_i V)},                 (2)

attained at y=0, uniquely whenever Q_i<V. Thus the maximum over the actual mixed set is max(Q_a,Q_b), with no restriction to axial or selected normals.

Write e=epsilon*c and parameterize ell_a=t>0, ell_b=t^(−2/3). Then

    Q(t)=max{min(1,1/2+e sqrt(t)),
             min(3/2,3/4+e sqrt(3/2)t^(−1/3))}.             (3)

The first unsaturated branch strictly increases in t and the second strictly decreases.

## 3. Exact small-epsilon optimum and escape rate

Define epsilon_* by

    epsilon_*^10=120^5/(221184*7^5).                        (4)

For 0<epsilon<epsilon_* there is a unique minimizer t_epsilon. Its value q_epsilon is the unique root in (3/4,1) of

    (q−1/2)^4(q−3/4)^6=(3/2)^3(epsilon*c)^10.              (5)

Indeed the left side is strictly increasing from zero to 1/65536 on that interval. At the root the two unsaturated branches of (3) meet, and any smaller or larger t increases one of them. Saturated branches cannot lower this value because their values are at least 1. The actual multiplier is

    ell_a=(q_epsilon−1/2)^2/(epsilon^2 c^2),
    ell_b=(q_epsilon−3/4)^2/((3/2)epsilon^2 c^2).            (6)

Equation (5) is exactly ell_a^2 ell_b^3=1. Both actual deepest points are the fiber midpoints; their own captured traces are proper because q_epsilon<1.

As epsilon decreases to zero, (5) gives q_epsilon→3/4. Therefore

    epsilon^2 ell_a→15/14,
    ell_b=ell_a^(−2/3)~(14/15)^(2/3)epsilon^(4/3),
    delta_a(0)→1/4,       delta_b(0)→0.                    (7)

Thus the optimized affine multiplier diverges at exactly the inverse-square scale. The buffer at the smaller fiber does NOT tend to zero. This happens at an attained positive, interior optimum for every small epsilon; it is not merely a nonattained boundary infimum.

The ordinary maximum depth of this body is b/2=3/4, attained only at base 1. The limiting optimized buffer elevates base 0 to that value while leaving its original ordinary depth 1/2 unchanged. It is therefore invalid to infer convergence of buffered deepest sets to ordinary deepest sets without uniform control of the physical buffer.

## 4. Nonproper own cuts can also occur

At epsilon=epsilon_*, equation (5) reaches q=1. The unique parameter meeting point has delta_a=1/2 and delta_b=1/4. The smaller fiber's buffered minimizing upper and lower cuts then contain its whole fiber, with a supporting boundary at its opposite endpoint. Its isolating pure-integer cap also has mass 1.

For epsilon>epsilon_*, choose the multiplier so that delta_b=1/4. Its normalization then forces delta_a>1/2, giving Q_a=Q_b=1. No value below 1 is possible: it would require both delta_a<1/2 and delta_b<1/4, contradicting the geometric-mean product (5) at this larger epsilon. Hence the optimum is exactly 1, and an optimizing multiplier has a full own trace at base 0. No regular-own-cut assertion follows from multiplier attainment alone.

## 5. Scope

The body is safe for OC: its ordinary raw maximum is 3/4, while the n=d=1 target is M/4=5/8. It is an affine-centroid graph and also has an endpoint heavier than M/2. The complement-face arithmetic theorem is unaffected; its stronger strict-minor assumptions are absent here.

The example isolates two logically distinct issues. Fixed-epsilon compactness/coercivity can yield an attained positive multiplier, while uniform control as epsilon tends to zero can fail. Even attained multiplier optima can have nonproper own cuts when the buffer is not quantitatively small.
